venue.name: Roy Henry Vickers Gallery
venue.description: Roy Henry Vickers Gallery is the artist's own gallery in downtown Tofino, built in 1986 with his family and carver Henry Nolla in the style of a traditional Northwest Coast longhouse with a carved and painted cedar plank exterior. Inside, paintings, original prints, art cards and reproductions hang on hand adzed cedar walls among totem poles and carvings, and the gallery is open free to the public all year round. On dates announced on the home page, Roy tells stories to guests gathered around the centre pit in the main hall and afterwards signs reproductions. The gallery and the business are currently listed for sale as Roy steps back from running them.
venue.hours_notes: Monday to Saturday: 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM. Sunday: 12:00 PM to 5:00 PM.

programs.name: Free gallery visit
programs.description: The gallery is open free to the public all year round, Monday to Saturday from 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM and Sunday from 12:00 PM to 5:00 PM. Nothing on the site describes a group visit, a group rate, a booking route for groups or a tour, so a group arrives the same way any other visitor does. On dates the site says are listed on the home page, Roy is at the gallery telling stories to guests around the centre pit in the main hall, and signs reproductions afterwards.
programs.what_children_do: Walk in past a carved cedar eagle on the front of the building, then look at paintings, original prints, art cards and carvings hung on hand adzed cedar walls among totem poles in the main hall. The room is quiet, with soft lighting and restful music playing. On a day when Roy is storytelling, guests gather around the centre pit in the main hall to listen.
programs.our_note: Everything on the walls is original art for sale, so this is a looking visit and not a touching one. It is one hall, quiet with soft lighting and music, which makes it a short stop rather than a morning out. The site says nothing at all about groups, so ring ahead and ask how many children they can take at once and whether you can use a washroom.
programs.practical_summary: Entry is free and indoors, in one hall in the middle of Tofino, and the address and opening hours are published. Washrooms, anywhere to eat, parking for a bus and whether a group needs to call first are not stated anywhere, so it is worth a phone call.
programs.evidence: The gallery is open free to the public all year round.

programs.name: Storytelling with Roy Henry Vickers at your event
programs.description: Roy can be booked to speak at an event away from the gallery. The site says he walks through selected works, shares the stories behind them and the life lessons passed on to him by his ancestors, and gets everyone involved in a sing-a-long or a traditional chant. No fee, audience age, group size or length is published, and the only booking route given is the gallery's email and phone number. The gallery and the business are listed for sale and Roy is stepping back from the business, so check this is still offered before planning around it.
programs.what_children_do: Sit and listen while Roy talks through a few of his works and tells the stories behind them, then join in a sing-along or a traditional chant.
programs.our_note: There is no price, no age guidance and no length anywhere on the site, so treat this as a conversation to start rather than something you can budget for. Ask what it costs, how long he speaks for, and whether he travels to you or the group has to come to him.
programs.practical_summary: Booking is by email or phone to the gallery and nothing else about it is published. The cost, the length, the youngest age it suits and where it can happen all have to be asked for.
programs.evidence: For more information on booking Roy to speak at your event please contact the gallery at tofino@royhenryvickers.com

gaps: No group price and no school or daycare rate is published. Entry to the gallery is free to everyone, but the site does not say whether a group has to pay anything, book, or give notice.

No youngest age is stated. The words school, field trip, group, tour, workshop, student, class, children and kids do not appear anywhere on the site in connection with visiting, including on the gallery page, the contact page, the policies page and the biography page. Both the school and daycare fields have been left blank rather than set to false, because the site gives no reason either way.
No limit on how many people can be in the gallery at once is published, so how large a group can be is unknown.
No lead time and no booking route for a group visit is published. The only contact given anywhere is the gallery's general phone number and email address.
Washrooms are not mentioned anywhere on the site.
Nowhere to eat is mentioned, indoors or out, and no nearby park is named.
Nothing is published about step-free entry, stroller access or wheelchair access.
Parking is not mentioned at all, and there is nothing about where a bus could stop or unload.

The gallery page says to check the home page for the dates Roy is storytelling, but no storytelling dates were listed on the home page when this was recorded, so those sessions cannot be planned around from the site.
The public speaking page publishes no fee, no audience age, no length, no group size and no travel area, only an email address and a phone number to ask.
The gallery and the business are advertised for sale on the site, with the owner stepping back from running it, so who runs it and what it offers may change.

RETRIEVAL NOTE: the site itself fetches fine and is not JavaScript rendered, but no browser was available in this run, so the photographs on the home page could not be recorded. They are CSS background images rather than img tags, and their content could not be identified without looking at them. The one image recorded is the only inline photograph in the body of the gallery page. It carries no alt text, and the alt written here rests on the page it sits on and on its file name rather than on viewing the image, so it should be checked by a person before publish.
